newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 22.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 22.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Australian Open tournament referee Peter Bellenger succumbed to the heat yesterday and closed the roof of Melbourne Park's Centre Court after angry calls from players that playing conditions were too dangerous. It was the first time in the history of Gran Slam tennis that the conditions of play were altered. Page 20.

After a disappointing first set, former Open champion Mary Pierce defeated the tenacious Sabine Appelmans 1-6, 6-4, 6-4, to win a place in the semi-finals against South African, Amanda Coetzer. Page 20.

Australian fast bowler Paul Reiffel passed his fitness examination yesterday for this week's fourth Test against the West Indies, but a turning Adelaide Oval may see selectors opt for the spin of Michael Bevan, leaving Reiffel and Test debutante Andy Bichel fighting for the final position. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Super League may be left without a national radio broadcaster after talks broke down with the ABC yesterday over the issue of Monday night football. The network wants to cover the night games, but Super League's television carrier, Channel Nine, has insised that there be no radio broadcast on the Monday night. Page 44.

The five heavy-weights of New South Wales rugby; Randwick, Gordon, Eastwood, Warringah and Easts, have united to express their disagreement with plans to alter this season's club competition. The five have attacked NSW Rugby Union's more "elitist focus" his year. Page 43.

Australian soccer national team players voted to take their pay dispute before the Industrial Relations Commission only hours before taking the field for their final game of the four-nations series in Sydney on Saturday night. The players are believed to ave voted 21-1 in favour of lodging their complaint with the Commission. Page 43.
THE AGE

Two young tennis players followed the lead of the Australian women's hockey team and donned ice jackets during breaks in their game at the Australian Open yesterday. Lleyton Hewitt and Nathan Healy wore the Australian Institute of Sport jackets to preventdehydration in their junior doubles match, which they won in three sets. Page C12.

Crowd favourites Mark Woodforde and Todd Woodbridge took to centre court in their victory against 10th seeds Damn and Olhovskiy in the quarter finals of the men's doubles yesterday. The Woodies played before a packed crowd, in what was the first doubles gme to be played on the centre court this tournament. Page C11.

Royal Melbourne looks set to be chosen as the venue for the 1998 Presidents Cup. The Cup, which will see the United States' 12 best golfers battle an International team of non-Europeans, will be the biggest tournament ever staged in Australia. Page C10.
THE HERALD SUN

Spanish heart-throb Carlos Moya advanced to the semi-finals of the Australian Open yesterday with a victory over country-man Felix Mantilla. It continued the 20-year-old's amazing run of form which started with last week's shock win against defending chapion Boris Becker. Page 76.

Argentinian Patricia Tarabini staged an on-going battle with the chair umpire in her doubles match yesterday, who she accused of laughing at her during her quarter finals match. The tantrum which lasted 10 minutes cost the player a point, and later A$100. Page 74.

Australian boxer Kostya Tszyu arrived home from Las Vegas yesterday after his controversial draw in the IBF world junior welterweight fight against Leonardo Mas. Mas was floored three times in the opening round, but the referee ruled the fight a technicaldraw after an unintentional illegal blow by Tszyu. Page 72.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

There have been calls within cricketing circles for former Australian cricket captain Greg Chappell to be installed as the new chief executive of the Australian Cricket Board. The speculation comes in the wake of Graham Halbish's controversial sacking last week. Page 78.

Super League will introduce a new judiciary system in its debut season this year by allotting points values to a variety of illegal tackles. In a system similar to current driving licence regulations, when a player passes a set points value, he will be auomatically suspended. Page 75.
Australian baseball player Dave Nilsson has been rewarded for an impressive season in America and has agreed to a new three-year deal with the Milwaukee Brewers. Page 73.
